title: Imports, scope, and self-containment
content: A single `import Mathlib` supplies the whole toolkit: matrix algebra, `minpoly`/`charpoly`, and the unique-factorization lemmas for `K[X]`. The 40-line docstring fixes this entry's position as sub-OQ-01 of the Jordan-Normal-Form problem and lists the deliverables — the shift power law, `N^d = 0`, the exact nilpotency index `N^(d-1) ≠ 0`, the Jordan–Chevalley split, and the minimal polynomial of a Jordan block. The key design decision, stated up front, is **self-containment**: `jordanBlock` is restated locally rather than imported from the ~500-line parent, so the file verifies against `Mathlib` alone and is immune to parent drift.
mathContext: Sub-OQ-01 / roadmap of minpoly-charpoly-oq-01. Deliverable: the spectral API of one Jordan block $\lambda I + N$.

title: The Jordan block and its nilpotent shift
content: `jordanBlock R λ d` is the `d × d` matrix with `λ` on the diagonal, `1` on the super-diagonal (entries `(i, i+1)`), and `0` elsewhere — encoded as a nested `if i = j then λ else if (j:ℕ) = (i:ℕ)+1 then 1 else 0`. Setting `λ = 0` gives the strict upper-shift `N`. The lemma `shift_apply` cleans up the `λ = 0` case: because the diagonal value is now `0`, the entry `(i,j)` collapses to the single condition `[(j:ℕ) = (i:ℕ)+1]`, absorbing the diagonal branch (when `i = j`, `(j:ℕ) ≠ (i:ℕ)+1`, so both descriptions give `0`).
mathContext: $\mathrm{jordanBlock}\,R\,\lambda\,d = \lambda I + N$, where $N_{ij} = [\,j = i+1\,]$ is the strict upper-shift.
prerequisites: Matrix as a function on Fin d × Fin d

title: Power law for the shift: (N^k) i j = [j = i + k]
content: The engine of the file. By induction on `k`: the base case `N^0 = 1` matches because `[i = j] = [(j:ℕ) = (i:ℕ) + 0]`; the step uses `pow_succ` (`N^(k+1) = N^k · N`) and `Matrix.mul_apply`. Right-multiplying by `N` means the only nonzero summand sits at column index `l = j - 1`, which — crucially — is *always* a valid `Fin d` element when it exists (`j ≥ 1`), so `Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem` collapses the sum cleanly. Multiplying on the *left* instead would force the surviving index to `i + 1`, which can overflow the block and fracture the proof into extra cases. When `(j:ℕ) = 0` every term vanishes and both sides are `0`.
mathContext: $N^k$ carries $1$s exactly on the $k$-th super-diagonal $\{(i, i+k)\}$; each power slides the band of $1$s one diagonal further toward the top-right corner.

title: N^d = 0 and IsNilpotent N
content: `shift_pow_dim_eq_zero` reads `N^d = 0` straight off the power law: the `d`-th power would place `1`s at positions `j = i + d`, but `j < d ≤ i + d`, so `omega` closes the impossibility and every entry is `0`. `isNilpotent_shift` then packages the witness `⟨d, shift_pow_dim_eq_zero⟩` into Mathlib's `IsNilpotent`. Both hold over an arbitrary commutative ring — nilpotency needs no field or nontriviality assumption.
mathContext: $N^d = 0$: at the $d$-th power the band of $1$s has been pushed entirely off the $d \times d$ matrix.

title: Sharpness: N^(d-1) ≠ 0
content: `shift_pow_pred_ne_zero` shows the nilpotency index is *exactly* `d`, not merely `≤ d`. The power law gives `(N^(d-1))` a `1` in the top-right corner `(0, d-1)` (since `(d-1) = 0 + (d-1)`), and over a `Nontrivial R` that `1 ≠ 0`, so the whole power is nonzero. This is the one place a nontriviality hypothesis is genuinely needed — over the zero ring every power is `0`. Paired with `N^d = 0`, this establishes the index precisely.
mathContext: $N^{d-1}$ leaves a single surviving $1$ at $(0, d-1)$, so it is nonzero: the nilpotency index of $N$ is exactly $d$.

title: Jordan–Chevalley split of one block: A - λI = N
content: `jordanBlock_sub_smul_one` proves `jordanBlock R λ d - λ • 1 = jordanBlock R 0 d` entrywise: on the diagonal `λ - λ·1 = 0`, on the super-diagonal `1 - λ·0 = 1`, elsewhere `0 - 0 = 0` — exactly the shift. This is the single-block instance of the semisimple + nilpotent (Jordan–Chevalley) decomposition, with `λI` the semisimple part and `N` the nilpotent part. Its corollary `sub_smul_one_pow_dim_eq_zero` rewrites `(A - λ•1)^d` to `N^d = 0`, transporting nilpotency to an arbitrary eigenvalue and feeding the minimal-polynomial argument.
mathContext: $A - \lambda I = N$: removing the scalar part of a Jordan block leaves the pure nilpotent shift; hence $(A - \lambda I)^d = 0$.

title: Minimal polynomial: minpoly K (jordanBlock K λ d) = (X - C λ)^d
content: The main result, a squeeze in three moves. (1) **Upper bound**: `aeval A ((X - C λ)^d) = (A - λ•1)^d = N^d = 0` (via `jordanBlock_sub_smul_one` + `shift_pow_dim_eq_zero`), so `minpoly.dvd` gives `minpoly K A ∣ (X - C λ)^d`. (2) **Shape**: `X - C λ` is prime (`prime_X_sub_C`), so `dvd_prime_pow` yields `Associated (minpoly K A) ((X - C λ)^m)` with `m ≤ d`; both polynomials are monic, so `eq_of_monic_of_associated` upgrades this to `minpoly K A = (X - C λ)^m`. (3) **Lower bound**: `minpoly.aeval` gives `(A - λ•1)^m = N^m = 0`; if `m < d` then `N^(d-1) = N^m · N^(d-1-m) = 0`, contradicting `shift_pow_pred_ne_zero`. Hence `m = d`. The upper bound is pure nilpotency, the lower bound pure sharpness, and primality is what converts divisibility into the exponent equality.
mathContext: $\mathrm{minpoly}_K(\lambda I + N) = (X - \lambda)^d = \mathrm{charpoly}$: the Jordan block is non-derogatory (cyclic).
